scenario.title: SECOND BATTLE OF KHARKOV - 12 MAY 1942
intro.text:
SECOND BATTLE OF KHARKOV - 12 MAY 1942

Volchansk, Northeast of Kharkov

We'll start an offensive to liberate Kharkov. With a dual pincer movement from the Volchansk and Barvenkovo salients, we'll surround and free the city. The main attack takes place in the south, your job is to lead the northern attack.

ORDERS
Kill 64 enemy units and prevent that the enemy destroy more than 15 of your units.

NOTES
Attention summer conditions! Don't forget to switch back to wheeled movement, if wanted.

CORE (recommended)
4x Tank (+1)
5x Infantry (+1)
2x Anti-Tank (+1)
2x Reconnaissance
1x Flak
4x Artillery
2x Fighter Aircraft
2x Tactical Bomber
header.act: ACT III — FROM DEFEAT TO OPERATIONAL MASTERY
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.reaction-briliant.text: Klin fell before the German retreat settled behind the railway. Success has made offensive arrows respectable again at headquarters.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.reaction-victory.text: The Moscow counteroffensive pushed the enemy from Klin. Our columns learned that pursuit in winter can exhaust the pursuer first.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.reaction-tactical.text: We crossed the railway and took Klin at the limit of the force. Headquarters sees momentum; the quartermasters see what it cost to keep moving.
line.callback-choice-a.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.callback-choice-a.text: You crossed the railway before the German retreat settled at Moscow. The forward detachments still trust your instinct for the unfinished moment.
line.callback-choice-b.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.callback-choice-b.text: You turned the railway into a supply line before entering Klin. That patience kept the guns with us. Headquarters has now drawn a plan that assumes patience belongs only to the enemy.
line.scene-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.scene-0.text: The situation map shows arrows meeting west of Kharkov. The intelligence annex shows German reserves whose locations are uncertain and road capacity that is not. The arrows are drawn in thicker ink.
line.scene-1.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.scene-1.text: I sent the reserve estimate three times. The first copy came back unsigned; the second was called pessimistic; the third is under Volkov's hand on this map.
line.scene-2.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.scene-2.text: The southern pincer is beyond our radio range, yet our orders assume its progress by the hour. We are being asked to make a local decision inside a plan whose other half we cannot see.
line.decision.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.decision.text: Command expects the northern pincer to keep advancing. We can commit fully to the timetable, or narrow the attack and preserve a reserve against the counterstroke our reconnaissance keeps reporting.
line.decision.choice.commit-to-the-pince: Drive the northern pincer on schedule and force the enemy to react to us.
Gain 120 prestige for accepting the full offensive commitment and give infantry and tanks 12 experience each; receive no resupply.
line.decision.choice.hold-a-mobile-reser: Narrow the first objective and keep a mobile reserve behind the salient.
Restore the core to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition and give reconnaissance formations 25 experience; reserve preparations cost 40 prestige.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-a-0.text: The timetable stands. Headquarters will not accept a smaller operation because its intelligence makes us uncomfortable.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.choice-a-1.text: Then leave my estimates attached to the lead group's orders. If the German reserves appear, nobody here will say the warning arrived afterward.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-b-0.text: The reserve remains out of the opening fight even if the first reports are favourable. Its purpose is to answer the event the plan did not predict.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.choice-b-1.text: Holding that reserve breaks the plan we were given. I will sign the change with you, Commander; Sokolova will not carry the blame alone if the southern pincer fails.
line.post-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.post-0.text: I will send the reserve estimate a fourth time. This copy carries both your signatures.
